Mick Porter was our next man but the rest of the team were much too far back to have any chance in the team race. This was won by Westbury Harriers with a good score of 73 points, with Portsmouth A.C. scoring 122, and Surrey A.C. third with 136.

Mick Porter finished 5th in the Doncaster to Sheffield Marathon Race on Easter Monday, which was run in very bad weather conditions. Bert Clayton was 3rd in the Inter-Counties 7 Miles Track Championship.

It was a pity that Mick Porter had to retire with shoe trouble as with 11 men in the first 81 positions he could have walked round to finish last and we should still have won the “Colman” Cup, which is awarded to the team with the lowest score for its complete team of 12 men.

We also gained third team awards in the Wigmore 15 miles road race on March 31st and Mick Porter was our first man home in 10th position. Mick Porter was also first home in 24th position in the Finchley 20 miles with Arthur Whitehead 39, Tom Carter 40, J.
Cornish (11), with Ian Forrester (8) second, and Gordon Lowers (5) third. The one mile handicap saw Mick Porter (130) run a good race to catch Tom Morrell (200) and A.
We did well in the 220 yards, with Merrett first and Alan Sexton third, while Ray Tooby won the half-mile and Mick Porter was third in the 1 mile.
"Ginger" Newell and Mick Porter came through well on the second lap with Maclean dropping back a bit and Hudson and Mike Stearman were too far back for us to stand a chance of getting placed.

The individual race was won easily by "Lofty" Holden, of Cambridge H., and our first man home was Bob Taylor, 17th, our other scorers being Mick Porter, 27; John Burr, 32; Ray Tooby, 38; Len Bishop, 57, and George Stace, 61.

In fairness to the Bishop brothers we must point out that Alan only came into our team at the last moment owing to the non-arrival of Mick Porter, while Len was spiked early in the race, and this must have affected his running.

Wal Wortley showed a most welcome return to form and it was pleasing to see our late member Mick Porter, now of Manchester, in such good shape. we did however, suffer a severe misfortune when Bert Jordan retired with tendon trouble after 15 miles.
Mick Porter, an old member of the cross-country section, has become the proud father of twins - making 4 children in all. Mick sends his regards to all his Belgrave friends.
Mick Porter and Lew Bush also ran well as did J.H.Braggington, who is a first season runner over the country.
We hear that Mike Porter, an active Belgravian in the late 1940's and early 1950's, is now treasurer of the Northern Veterans' A.C. and still clocking around 64 minutes for ten miles.
